note.note:
Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure: Painful, cracked, itchy skin on palms; symptoms began ~4 months ago after starting new housekeeping job using cleaning chemicals without gloves.
- Symptom timeline and progression: Gradual onset over months, recently worsened to the point patient missed last 3 days of work.
- ENT symptoms: Denies throat swelling/closure sensation, voice change, dysphagia/odynophagia, drooling, nasal/ocular symptoms, stridor/noisy breathing, dyspnea, facial/lip/tongue/uvular swelling, ear pain/hearing changes, neck pain/swelling.
- Relevant past episodes and treatments: First occurrence. Tried OTC emollient (E45) and an unspecified antihistamine—no relief. No prior ED visits or injection therapy.
- Allergies and current medications:
  • No known drug or other allergies.
  • Metformin (dose/route/frequency not documented).
  • OTC E45 cream (as needed; ineffective).
  • Unspecified oral antihistamine (dose/route/frequency not documented; ineffective).
- Social context: Works as a hotel housekeeper; inconsistent glove use; currently off work 3 days due to pain.

Objective:
- Observable swelling and distribution: Patient reports cracked, dry, itchy palms; no bleeding unless scratched.
- Airway/breathing: No airway or respiratory complaints.
- Mental status/associated features: No systemic symptoms; afebrile per history.
- Vitals and examination findings: Not recorded.
- Presence of another person: Not stated.

Assessment:
- Likely irritant / occupational contact dermatitis of the palms secondary to repeated exposure to cleaning chemicals without glove protection.
  Justification: Onset corresponds with new housekeeping role; localized to areas of contact; chronic dryness/cracking; absence of systemic or ENT-related manifestations.

Plan:
- Immediate actions/advice:
  • Prescription topical moderate-potency corticosteroid cream (specific product and dosing not documented) for inflamed areas.
  • Prescribe/advise use of “stronger” emollient; apply generously 3–4 times daily for 2 weeks.
  • Strict glove use with all cleaning tasks; minimize contact with detergents/chemicals.
- Escalation/red-flag advice:
  • Return sooner if rash spreads, pain/cracking worsens, signs of infection occur, or functional impairment increases.
- Follow-up:
  • Routine review in 10–14 days to assess response.
  • Earlier review if deterioration.
  • Consider alternative therapies or referral to dermatology/occupational health if no improvement.
- Education:
  • Importance of consistent protective measures and skin hydration.
  • Continue diabetes management as usual.

Quality checks (document_quality):
• Missing/expected details: ENT exam findings, vitals, steroid cream name/dose/frequency, antihistamine specifics, formal allergy list beyond “none,” documentation of auto-injector or anaphylaxis plan (not applicable but typical for ENT-allergy visits).  
• Internal conflicts: None noted.  
• Transcript quality: Clear; no significant inaudible segments.
